3. The facts as has been stated, in short, is that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 85 of 2001 on 24.07.2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Lohagora, Narail against the predecessors of the opposite parties as defendants praying for a decree of declaration that the disputed sale deed No. 1802 dated 08.02.1975 in respect of the suit land as described in the schedule to the plaint is forged, fabricated, without consideration and not binding upon her. The said Title Suit No. 85 of 2001 was dismissed for default by Order No. 37 dated 06.10.2005. It may be mentioned here that earlier also the suit was dismissed for default by an order dated 21.09.2003. The said suit was restored to its file and number by judgment and order dated 10.05.2005 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 2003 under Order IX rule 9 of the Code of  Civil Procedure filed by the plaintiff-petitioner. After dismissal of the suit for default on 06.10.2005, the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005 under Order IX rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for restoration of the suit to its original file and number after setting aside the Order dated 06.10.2005 dismissing the suit for default. In the said Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005 the petitioner inadvertently made the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 as opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 though they were dead. Consequently, the petitioner filed an application on 14.02.2006 in the said case for striking out the names of the opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 substituting their heirs. By Order No. 41 dated 14.02.2006 the application was allowed. By Order No. 51 dated 06.03.2007 the said Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005 dated 06.03.2007 was allowed and the suit was restored to its original file and number. 

 4. After restoration of the suit an application for recording abatement of the suit in the name of the dead defendant Nos. 1 and 3 and the defendant No. 4 was filed on 16.09.2009. The plaintiff (petitioner herein) also filed an application on 24.09.2009 praying for recording the names of the heirs of the defendant 'Nos. I to 3 in the suit as they had already been substituted in Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005. The plaintiff (petitioner herein) also filed another application on the same day that is on 24.09.2009, praying for substitution of the heirs of the substituted defendant No. 2(Ka), late Abul Kalam Azad who died on 02.07.2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court, after hearing both the parties by his order No. 80 dated 15.10,2009 was pleased to reject to the applications for recording abatement dated 16.09.2009 and allowed both the applications for substitution. 

 6. Mr. Md. Delwar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing with Ms. Selma Begum, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the learned District Judge, committed an error of law in allowing the Civil Revision holding that the heirs of the defendants were not substituted in Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005, however, the Order dated 14.02.2006, it appears that the heirs of the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 were allowed to be substituted. He next submitted that the teamed Judge while allowing the Civil Revision has observed - that since the defendant No. 2 died long before, yet the plaintiff did not take any steps to substitute the heirs of the defendant No. 2 but from the order dated 14.02.2006 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005, it appears that the heirs of the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 were allowed to be substituted and thus the learned District Judge committed an error of law in his decision occasioning failure of justice and thus the impugned judgment and order is liable to he set aside. 

 7. He further submitted that the heirs of the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 were substituted by an order dated 14.02.2006 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005 and the heirs of the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 did not approach the higher Court against the said order, and as such, the said order is binding upon the heirs of the defendant Nos. 1 and 3 but the teamed District Judge without considering the same committed an error of law. 

 9. He also submitted that Abul Kalam Azad, the substituted heir of the defendant No. 2 died on 02.07.2009 and an application for substitution of his heirs was filed on 24.09.2009, that is well within 90 days, and as such, the question abatement of the suit does not arise at all. Furthermore, neither of the substituted heirs of the defendant No. 2 including Abul Kalam Azad contested the original suit and the Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005, who did not even file the instant Civil Revision. But the learned District Judge without applying his judicial mind allowed the instant Civil Revision. 

 11. On perusal of the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the documents annexed to the application the pivotal issue is with regard to substitution of the heirs of the deceased-defendant Nos. 1 to 3. On perusal of the documents submitted with the petition it is found that the deceased defendant Nos. 1 to 3 were duly substituted in course of time in the miscellaneous case filed under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 14.02.2006, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge, Narail dated 28.04.2011 thereby reversing the judgment and order dated 15.10.2009 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Lohagara, Narail in Title Suit No. 85 of 2001 is found to be unjustified and therefore the Rule attracts merit.
